distinguishing_features: Fixed micro-lamella array with micro-textured walls creating stationary high-shear nucleation zones
Decoupling nucleation site (stationary surface) from crystal growth environment (bulk shear) to shear ice off before it grows thick
Active sweeping of bulk flow across nucleation sites to prevent solute accumulation at sites
Ice-detachment-by-shear mechanism keeping transient ice boundary layer thin (<10 um) for continuous solute rejection
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent growing ice from forming a thick solute-trapping layer on cooling surfaces while maintaining adequate heat transfer during freeze-concentration of juice.
parsed.viable_reason: The shear-stress balance (~10 Pa vs 5-15 Pa adhesion) and micro-channel geometry are physically plausible at the stated scale, enabling continuous ice detachment and solute rejection.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art uses pulsed flow modulation of existing loops; pinning nucleation to micro-textured surfaces and shearing off ice to decouple nucleation from growth is a distinct structural step, not a routine parameter change.
